read_only_inputs_note: ow_tp.silver.invoices is silver_invoicing's target and is read-only here: it supplies the status_cd = 40 population fn_overdue_accounts, sp_schedule_dunning and sp_suspend_overdue all drive from. ow_tp.bronze.tenants is bronze_core's target and is read-only here; this unit's tenant-status output goes to ow_tp.silver.tenants and never back to bronze.

quarantine_reason_notes.NUMERIC_OVERFLOW: a reachable guard, evaluated on every attempt row (attempt_no outside INT, |invoice_total| beyond DECIMAL(14,2)) and reported every run. The attempt half does fire: the scheduled attempt_no is NVL(MAX(attempt_no),0)+1, computed in BIGINT so the candidate can be judged before anything casts it, and an invoice whose highest existing attempt is INT_MAX yields a candidate outside the target's INT — exercised in ns=dunning_edge. The money half cannot be reached from ow_tp.bronze.dunning_attempts or ow_tp.silver.invoices, whose columns are already INT and DECIMAL(14,2), so it is reported as measured rather than presented as a detection.

quarantine_reasons_declared_unreachable.BAD_DATE: no VARCHAR2 date reaches this unit: DUNNING_ATTEMPTS.scheduled_for is a DATE and NOTIFICATIONS.sent_at a TIMESTAMP, both already typed in bronze
quarantine_reasons_declared_unreachable.DATE_INVALID: same as BAD_DATE — no string date is parsed here
quarantine_reasons_declared_unreachable.AMT_NON_NUMERIC: no fixed-width or text money field reaches this unit; the only money it carries is INVOICES.total, already DECIMAL(14,2) in silver
quarantine_reasons_declared_unreachable.ENC_INVALID: no byte-positional feed reaches this unit; federated text passes through unchanged (D-25)

quarantine_halt_bases.dunning_attempts: attempt driver: one row per source OW_BILLING.DUNNING_ATTEMPTS row in ns, plus one row per status_cd = 40 invoice sp_schedule_dunning's cursor visits in this run — numerator and denominator on that one population
quarantine_halt_bases.tenants: tenants: every OW_BILLING.TENANTS row in ns — numerator and denominator on that one population
quarantine_halt_bases.notifications: notification driver: one row per source OW_BILLING.NOTIFICATIONS row in ns, plus one row per suspension notification sp_suspend_overdue's NOT EXISTS lets through in this run — numerator and denominator on that one population
quarantine_halt_bases.subscriptions_swept: shared-table driver: one row per ow_tp.silver.subscriptions row in ns that sp_suspend_overdue's UPDATE matches in this run (tenant swept, subscription at status_cd = 10) — numerator and denominator on that one population

quarantine_halt_basis_note: each declared population is evaluated against the threshold with its own paired numerator and denominator, and the unit halts if any one of them exceeds it: tolerance item 5 forbids diluting a population, not evaluating all of them. Phase 1 evaluates dunning_attempts, phase 2 evaluates tenants, notifications and subscriptions_swept; a halt in phase 1 stops phase 2 through the task dependency, and quarantine rows are persisted before either evaluation (tolerance item 6). The comparison is rejected_rows * 100 > threshold_pct * source_rows on the unrounded pair; rate_pct is rounded to four decimals for reading only, so a population at 5.00004% halts although it displays as 5.0.

quarantine_ledger_identity.note: _batch_id is part of the identity rather than a column the MERGE overwrites, so a rejection that recurs on a later night becomes that night's own ledger row and an earlier batch keeps the rows its own halt was evaluated on (tolerance item 3). source_key carries an occurrence ordinal, so two physical rejected rows sharing a natural key and reason are two ledger rows with their own payloads rather than one row standing for both — including bronze tenant rows the id de-duplication collapses before the sweep join, which are rejected individually rather than only counted. A retry of the same batch matches on the same identity and refreshes the payload columns, so it is idempotent.

dunning_constants.day_abbreviation_source: TO_CHAR(dt, 'DY', 'NLS_DATE_LANGUAGE=ENGLISH') — reproduced by indexing this array with dayofweek(dt) (1 = SUN .. 7 = SAT), whose origin day the notebook proves against pinned dates before it is used; date_format(dt,'EEE') is never emitted (D-24)
dunning_constants.overdue_predicate: date_format(issued_at,'yyyyMMdd') < date_format(as_of,'yyyyMMdd') — strictly less than, so an invoice issued earlier on the same calendar day is not overdue (D-07)
dunning_constants.schedule_predicate: status_cd = 40 only: sp_schedule_dunning's cursor carries no date filter at all, so it visits every overdue invoice, including one issued today that fn_overdue_accounts excludes
dunning_constants.days_overdue_expr: datediff(trunc(as_of), trunc(issued_at)) — Oracle TRUNC(p_as_of) - TRUNC(CAST(i.issued_at AS DATE)), an integer day count on truncated dates
dunning_constants.attempt_no_expr: coalesce(max(attempt_no), 0) + 1 per invoice_id (NVL(MAX(attempt_no),0)+1), evaluated set-wise in BIGINT over the ingest attempt population plus this unit's own target rows from strictly earlier as_of values. The earlier-as_of half is what makes the next night append attempt n+1 instead of merging over the previous night's row; excluding this run's own as_of is what makes a rerun of the same night recompute the same ids and change nothing (DIV-RERUN-APPENDS). A candidate outside the target's INT is quarantined NUMERIC_OVERFLOW before any cast.
dunning_constants.suspended_on_expr: TRUNC(p_as_of) — the truncated date, not the run timestamp

job.name: ow_tp_silver_dunning
job.compute: serverless (no job_clusters, no instance pools, no warehouse created)
job.batch_id: {{job.run_id}} — one batch id for both tasks, which is how phase 2 finds the snapshot phase 1 wrote

invoice_source_policy.silver: ow_tp.silver.invoices, silver_invoicing's target, read-only: the population every namespace holding migrated source data drives from
invoice_source_policy.bronze: ow_tp.bronze.invoices, used only by a declared generated-fixture namespace. Seeding fixture invoices into ow_tp.silver.invoices would mean writing another unit's silver target, which this unit is forbidden even in a scratch namespace, so the fixture's invoices are generated in bronze and the notebook reads them there. The only difference is the FROM clause; the recon report declares it as an unverified path for that namespace.

fixture_namespaces.dunning_edge: generated fixture, declared as generated: exercises the populations the demo seed leaves at zero (a missing tenant row kept by the outer join, an UNKNOWN tenant status, a same-calendar-day invoice, subscriptions left at 20 and at 30, a tenant already carrying a suspension notification on another date, an existing attempt at INT_MAX so the attempt derived from it overflows the target's INT, and each reachable quarantine reason) with enough clean rows that no population crosses the 5% halt. No row of it is customer history and it never writes ns=demo or ns=plans_edge (wave 3's fixture namespace).
fixture_namespaces.dunning_halt: generated fixture whose attempt population is deliberately more than 5% rejects, used once to show the halt actually fires and that the rejected rows are already persisted when it does.

contract_inaccuracies_reported_upstream.contract_says: notification rows written as a side effect of the sweep, with no idempotency key in source, so a legacy rerun duplicates them
contract_inaccuracies_reported_upstream.source_actually_does: the INSERT carries WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM notifications WHERE tenant_id = t.tenant_id AND kind_cd = 3 AND sent_at = CAST(TRUNC(p_as_of) AS TIMESTAMP)), and uq_notifications (tenant_id, kind_cd, sent_at) backs it: a legacy rerun on the same p_as_of adds nothing. What a rerun on a *different* p_as_of adds is a second notification for a tenant still at status_cd = 10 — and the sweep's own UPDATE TENANTS SET status_cd = 20 takes the tenants it just suspended out of that population.
contract_inaccuracies_reported_upstream.resolution: the source is reproduced, not the contract's description; the contract file is not edited by this unit and the inaccuracy is reported to the parent session for a central decision

one_snapshot_policy.rule: JOB_NIGHTLY_DUNNING runs sp_schedule_dunning then sp_suspend_overdue inside one job action, over one state of the invoice population. The target is one job with two ordered notebook tasks (schedule_dunning -> suspend_overdue, depends_on) in one run. Phase 1 persists the overdue snapshot once, as JSON under the run's ns-scoped volume path; phase 2 reads that file and never re-queries ow_tp.silver.invoices for its population. Phase 2 fails closed if the snapshot file for its batch is absent.
one_snapshot_policy.snapshot_population: every ow_tp.silver.invoices row in ns with status_cd = 40, carrying the three source predicates as columns (in_schedule_driver, overdue_by_fn, in_suspend_cutoff), days_overdue, the DECODE tenant_status, and the invoice total

shared_write_policy.audit_columns_note: D-30 allows the updating unit its own audit columns, but adding one to ow_tp.silver.subscriptions is DDL on another unit's table, which this unit is forbidden. So no column is added and no column outside updatable_columns is written; the per-row evidence (which ids were updated, their prior status_cd, and the count) lives in the recon report and in this unit's own ow_tp.silver.tenants rows instead.
forbidden: DDL (CREATE/ALTER/DROP, including adding an audit column)
writing starts_on, ends_on, plan_id, tenant_id, status_cd_before, closed_by_change, closeout_seq or any other silver_plans column
shared_write_policy.attribution_precondition: every matched row must carry an _origin this unit recognises as a merged unit's and a non-empty _batch_id; a matched row that does not is not resolved locally — the unit raises and reports centrally
shared_write_policy.no_delete_note: this unit issues no DELETE at all, on any table. D-31's carve-out covers rows a unit generated itself under a job input it no longer accepts; this unit's driver is the source's own overdue population, so no row it writes qualifies (D-28, D-31). Separately, and outside the deployed job: the validation harness under scripts/tp_databricks/silver_dunning/ does DELETE this unit's own rows in the namespace it reconciles, to make the recon report's cold load cold after earlier validation runs. That is harness setup, it is published in the report's reconciled_namespace_setup, and no notebook the job runs contains a DELETE.

declared_divergences.source: WHEN OTHERS THEN NULL around the attempt INSERT in sp_schedule_dunning, with g_scheduled_cnt incremented only on success
declared_divergences.target: no swallow: an attempt this unit cannot write fails the unit loudly, and an attempt the source could not have written is quarantined with its closed reason code and counted
declared_divergences.measured: attempts the source's handler would have swallowed, by cause (FK_ORPHAN on the missing tenant row, KEY_DUPLICATE on uq_dunning_attempts), reported in the recon report

declared_divergences.source: sp_schedule_dunning re-run on the same p_as_of reads NVL(MAX(attempt_no),0)+1 from a DUNNING_ATTEMPTS table its own previous run already grew, so it appends another attempt per overdue invoice on every run. Two *concurrent* runs are the other half of it: the SELECT takes no lock, both read the same MAX, both build the same f_md5_uuid(invoice_id || attempt_no) id, and the loser's ORA-00001 is swallowed by WHEN OTHERS THEN NULL while g_scheduled_cnt already claims the row.
declared_divergences.target: attempt numbering is pinned set-wise to the ingest attempt population (ow_tp.bronze.dunning_attempts) plus this unit's own rows from earlier as_of values, so the ids are a function of (ns, as_of, ingest state): a rerun of the same night is a true no-op, and a genuinely later night appends attempt n+1 the way a later source night would
declared_divergences.measured: attempts a source rerun would append, per run

declared_divergences.source: trg_subscriptions_hist writes one SUBSCRIPTIONS_HIST row per subscription sp_suspend_overdue updates, with HIST_DT as a 'DD-MON-YY HH24:MI:SS' string
declared_divergences.target: retired: no _HIST write from the target. Delta history covers the change instead.

declared_divergences.source: g_last_run_dt and g_scheduled_cnt are package state, and pkg_ow_util.log_msg reports the count from an autonomous transaction
declared_divergences.target: carried as explicit run-level output fields (as_of, scheduled_count) in the run summary and the recon report, not as package state; BILLING_AUDIT_LOG stays out of parity scope (D-20)

columns.name: id
columns.note: f_md5_uuid(invoice_id || TO_CHAR(attempt_no)) for rows this run schedules; the ingest id for migrated rows (D-14)

columns.name: status
columns.note: CODES('DUN_STATUS') description of status_cd

columns.name: as_of
columns.note: the run's TRUNC(p_as_of), carried on every row this run judged, migrated rows included, so the whole slice states which night's state it holds

columns.name: attempt_no_basis
columns.note: NVL(MAX(attempt_no),0) the numbering read for this invoice; NULL on migrated rows

columns.name: source_day_of_week
columns.note: the English NLS day abbreviation of TRUNC(p_as_of), the value the source DECODE compares

columns.name: weekend_shift_days
columns.note: 0, 1 or 2 — the DECODE's shift, so ANOM-LOCALE-DAY is evidenced per row

columns.name: unshifted_scheduled_for
columns.note: TRUNC(p_as_of) before the weekend shift

columns.name: invoice_total
columns.note: the driving invoice's total, an audit column and not a source column of DUNNING_ATTEMPTS: it carries the money of the population this unit drives from so parity is exact to the cent on a Delta target (T1)

columns.name: overdue_by_fn
columns.note: true when fn_overdue_accounts' strictly-less-than predicate holds; sp_schedule_dunning's cursor has no date filter, so a same-day invoice is false here and still scheduled

columns.name: tenant_status
columns.note: the DECODE(t.status_cd,...) value, 'UNKNOWN' for a missing or unmapped tenant row (D-03, D-18)

columns.name: id
columns.note: f_md5_uuid(tenant_id || 'suspension' || TO_CHAR(TRUNC(p_as_of),'YYYY-MM-DD')) for rows this run writes; the ingest id for migrated rows (D-14)

columns.name: kind
columns.note: CODES('NOTIF_KIND') description of kind_cd

columns.name: tenant_status_before
columns.note: the tenant status the sweep's IF v_active > 0 test read

columns.name: status_cd
columns.note: the status after the sweep: 20 where the sweep suspended the tenant, otherwise the ingest status

columns.name: status_cd_ingest
columns.note: the ow_tp.bronze.tenants status this unit read; the sweep's UPDATE TENANTS SET status_cd = 20 is expressed as this column plus status_cd, never as a write back to bronze

columns.name: sweep_candidate
columns.note: in the DISTINCT tenant_id cursor: has a status_cd = 40 invoice issued on or before TRUNC(p_as_of) - 14

columns.name: skipped_inactive_at_ingest
columns.note: a sweep candidate whose ingest status was not 10, so IF v_active > 0 was false and the source did nothing for it

columns.name: subscriptions_suspended
columns.note: a state count, not a delta: this tenant's ow_tp.silver.subscriptions rows that stand at status_cd = 20 with suspended_on = TRUNC(p_as_of) once this run's matched updates are applied. Counting only the rows this run changed would fall to zero on a rerun, which would make the rerun a change rather than a no-op (ACC-IDEM); a row already suspended on this same date by ingest is therefore counted here too.

columns.name: subscriptions_left_suspended
columns.note: at status_cd = 20 with a suspended_on other than TRUNC(p_as_of) — suspended before this night and left alone

columns.name: subscriptions_left_cancelled
columns.note: at status_cd = 30, left alone — also the trg_sub_no_uncancel rule (D-16)
